author: JakeGamer2000
what_it_is: Ultimate 100% save, all coin collected in all courses, 120 star, all cap switch opened, all area unlocked, basically maxed out all the game needed, including 192rd impossible coin in Tiny-Huge island
format: a DexDrive .n64 made by savefileconverter.com (comment 0 says so; header otherwise zero; ID block with that tool's random serial pattern; index-table checksum byte 0): one cart-save note "SUPER MARIO 64" (3BADD1E5/FADE), 8 pages = the 4 Kbit EEPROM padded to 2048 bytes

verified.converted_with: tools/gamefaqs/n64-dexdrive.py convert super-mario-64.31112.n64 OUT: dexdrive: pak = the 32768 bytes after the 0x1040-byte header; cart-save note 'SUPER MARIO 64' (GameShark 3BADD1E5/FADE): raw EEPROM, 2048 bytes

converted_standalone.how: the same bytes as the .srm regions, as standalone Mupen64Plus keeps them: <GoodName (32 chars)>-<MD5 8>.eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk in its save folder

verified.baseline: with no save: SELECT FILE, all four files NEW

mupen64plus-next.detail: SELECT FILE: MARIO A 120 stars, B-D NEW

parallel-n64.detail: SELECT FILE: MARIO A 120 stars, B-D NEW

mupen64plus.detail: SELECT FILE: MARIO A 120 stars, B-D NEW

note: Not written by a DexDrive: savefileconverter.com wrote it (its comment says so) from a 4 Kbit EEPROM of unknown origin, padding it to 2048 bytes. The pak it built has a 00 index-table checksum, which libultra would treat as inconsistent; only the EEPROM is used here.
